key_insight: Learning from overlapping patches of a single turbulent realization enables extreme ×32 and ×64 super-resolution of previously unseen flow fields.
engineering_relevance: This data-efficient approach could help reconstruct under-resolved turbulent flows when high-resolution training data are scarce.
method: Train a wide-activation deep super-resolution (WDSR) network on overlapping patches from one high-resolution realization.
Predict unseen fields patchwise and assemble them using Hann-window-weighted overlap-add.
Compare against interpolation and WDSR models trained on 1, 25, 50, or 100 complete snapshots.
evidence_signal: In two-dimensional homogeneous isotropic turbulence at ×32 and ×64, the abstract reports improved vortical structures, fine-scale features, and high-wavenumber energy recovery relative to interpolation.
watch_item: Validation is limited to two-dimensional homogeneous isotropic turbulence; transfer to three-dimensional or more complex engineering flows remains unestablished.
paper_title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization
